📚 Today you learned

Fiscal Quarter vs. Calendar Quarter Offset

Not every company's "Q3" means July-September. NVDA's fiscal year starts in late January, so the quarter it reports Aug 26 is "Q2 FY2027" even though calendar-wise it's mostly May-July. AVGO's fiscal year starts in November, so what it reports Sep 2 is "Q3 FY2026" — a totally different calendar window than NVDA's Q2. This trips people up coming from forex/indices, where everything is calendar-quarter. The practical fix: never assume "Q3" lines up across two tickers — check the actual date range each company covers before comparing YoY growth rates or building a sector-wide earnings calendar. Semis and retailers are the most common offenders; banks and most large-caps use calendar fiscal years.

Also today: Guidance range vs. point estimate — NVDA guides revenue as "$91.0B ±2%," a band, not a single number; a beat only counts if the actual print clears the top of the band, not just the midpoint.
